Hazor-hadattah
HAY-zor hah-DAT-tah
proper noun
Hebrew Chatsor Chadattah, “New Hazor,” a town in the far south of Judah toward the border of Edom, distinct from the great Hazor of the north.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Hazor-hadattah means “New Hazor,” a small town in the parched southland of Judah, named once in the roll of the tribe’s uttermost cities: “And Hazor, Hadattah, and Kerioth, and Hezron, which is Hazor” (Jos 15:25). It lay among “the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward” (Jos 15:21), in the dry Negeb where several towns bore the name Hazor, so that one was distinguished as New Hazor and another as Hazor which is Hezron. This is no famed Hazor of Jabin and the northern wars, but an obscure settlement of the desert frontier. The whole southern list belongs to Judah’s inheritance: “This then was the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families; even to the border of Edom the wilderness of Zin southward” (Jos 15:1). Hazor-hadattah preaches, like all these forgotten border-towns, the faithful particularity of God. He did not overlook the arid edge of the land, the smallest hamlet toward Edom; He named it and gave it. The lines fell for Judah even in the wilderness of Zin, and the goodly heritage reached to the farthest, driest corner. What the world would pass over as barren and unimportant, the LORD wrote in the book of the inheritance, for He forgets none of His people’s portion, however small or however dry.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

“New Hazor,” an obscure town in the far south of Judah toward Edom (Jos 15:25), distinct from the great northern Hazor; a witness to God’s faithful particularity to the last dry corner of the inheritance.

HAZOR-HADATTAH, “New Hazor,” a town in the far south of Judah.

Named once, in the uttermost cities toward Edom (Jos 15:25).

Distinct from the great Hazor of Jabin in the north.

One of several Negeb towns bearing the name Hazor.

A witness to God’s care for the least corner of the inheritance.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 15:25 — "And Hazor, Hadattah, and Kerioth, and Hezron, which is Hazor,"

Jos 15:21 — "And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,"

Jos 15:1 — "This then was the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families; even to the border of Edom the wilderness of Zin southward"

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

“New Hazor” of the southern desert; the entry recovers God’s faithful particularity to the least and driest corner of His people’s inheritance.

expand to see more

Hazor-hadattah faces no modern redefinition; it is scarcely known. Yet its lone mention in the desert list rebukes the worldly measure that counts only the fertile and the famous worth recording. God named New Hazor on the arid edge toward Edom and folded it into Judah’s inheritance.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the tender exactness of God’s covenant faithfulness. He did not stop His reckoning at the pleasant valleys but ran the lines to the wilderness of Zin, naming the smallest hamlet of the parched frontier. The lines fell for Judah even there, and the heritage was called goodly (Psa 16:6). So the believer’s portion in Christ reaches to every corner of his life, even the dry and barren places the world despises. God forgets no part of what He has given His own.
